question:
A bus moving on a straight road at a speed of 10 km/h increases its speed to 70 km/h in 2 minutes. Find its average acceleration.

[RRB NTPC CBT]
options: 1 km/minute2
0.5 km/minute2
2 km/minute2
30 km/minute2
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is 0.5 km/minute2

Explanation:
Acceleration is defined as the rate of change of velocity. The formula for average acceleration is:
[ text{Average acceleration} = frac{text{Change in velocity}}{text{Time interval}} ]
Here, initial velocity (u) = 10 km/h, final velocity (v) = 70 km/h, and time (t) = 2 minutes.
Change in velocity = v - u = 70 - 10 = 60 km/h
Since time is given in minutes and the answer is required in km/minute2, we do not need to convert time into hours.
[ text{Average acceleration} = frac{60 text{ km/h}}{2 text{ minutes}} = 30 text{ km/h per minute} ]
But the options are given in km/minute2, so we convert it:
1 hour = 60 minutes, so:
[ 30 text{ km/h per minute} = frac{30}{60} text{ km/minute}^2 = 0.5 text{ km/minute}^2 ]

Extra Facts:
Acceleration is a vector quantity, and its SI unit is meter/second2 (m/s2). It is related to Newton's Second Law of Motion, which states that Force (F) = Mass (m) × Acceleration (a). Acceleration can be positive (increase in speed) or negative (deceleration or decrease in speed). In real life, acceleration is used to measure changes in speed in vehicles, rockets, and sports.

Important one-liners for upcoming exams

☛ What is the formula of Newton's Second Law? → F = ma
☛ What is negative acceleration called? → Retardation
☛ What is the value of gravitational acceleration? → 9.8 m/s2
☛ What is the acceleration of an object moving with uniform velocity? → Zero
question_hi:
सीधी सड़क पर 10 km/h की चाल से गति करती हुई एक बस 2 मिनट में अपनी चाल 70 km/h तक बढ़ा देती है। बस का औसत त्वरण (acceleration) ज्ञात कीजिए।

[RRB NTPC CBT]
options_hi: 1 किमी/ वर्ग मिनट
0.5 किमी/वर्ग मिनट
2 किमी/वर्ग मिनट
30 किमी/वर्ग मिनट
solution_hi:
हल: सही उत्तर है 0.5 किमी/वर्ग मिनट

Explanation:
त्वरण (acceleration) को वेग में परिवर्तन की दर के रूप में परिभाषित किया जाता है। औसत त्वरण की गणना निम्न सूत्र द्वारा की जाती है:
[ text{औसत त्वरण} = frac{text{वेग में परिवर्तन}}{text{समय अंतराल}} ]
यहाँ, प्रारंभिक वेग (u) = 10 km/h, अंतिम वेग (v) = 70 km/h, और समय (t) = 2 मिनट।
वेग में परिवर्तन = v - u = 70 - 10 = 60 km/h
समय को मिनट में दिया गया है, इसलिए इसे घंटे में बदलने की आवश्यकता नहीं है क्योंकि त्वरण की इकाई किमी/वर्ग मिनट में मांगी गई है।
[ text{औसत त्वरण} = frac{60 text{ km/h}}{2 text{ मिनट}} = 30 text{ km/h per minute} ]
लेकिन यहाँ विकल्पों में किमी/वर्ग मिनट दिया गया है, इसलिए हमें इसे किमी/मिनट2 में बदलना होगा।
1 घंटा = 60 मिनट, इसलिए:
[ 30 text{ km/h per minute} = frac{30}{60} text{ km/minute}^2 = 0.5 text{ km/minute}^2 ]

Extra Facts:
त्वरण एक सदिश राशि है, जिसका मात्रक एसआई (SI) पद्धति में मीटर/सेकंड2 (m/s2) होता है। यह गति के दूसरे नियम (न्यूटन का दूसरा नियम) से संबंधित है, जिसके अनुसार बल (F) = द्रव्यमान (m) × त्वरण (a)। त्वरण धनात्मक (गति बढ़ने पर) या ऋणात्मक (मंदन या गति कम होने पर) हो सकता है। वास्तविक जीवन में, त्वरण का उपयोग वाहनों, रॉकेट, और खेलों में गति परिवर्तन को मापने के लिए किया जाता है।

question:
Which Law of Newton states that for every action (force) in nature there is an equal and opposite reaction ?

[SSC GD 2024]
options: 2nd
1st
4th
3rd
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is 3rd

Explanation:
Newton's Third Law of Motion states that "For every action, there is an equal and opposite reaction." This means that when one object exerts a force on another, the second object exerts an equal and opposite force on the first. For example, when we push the ground with our feet (action), the ground pushes back with an equal force (reaction), enabling us to walk. This law explains propulsion in rockets and swimming motions.

Extra Facts:
- Newton's three laws of motion are: First Law (Law of Inertia), Second Law (F = ma), and Third Law (Action-Reaction).
- This law is linked to the principle of conservation of momentum, as the net force of action-reaction pairs is zero.
- Applications include jet engines, rockets, and the recoil of a gun.

Important one-liners for upcoming exams

☛ What is the SI unit of force? → Newton (N)
☛ What is the formula for momentum? → Mass × Velocity
☛ What is Newton's Second Law formula? → F = ma
☛ On which principle does a rocket work? → Newton's Third Law
question_hi:
न्यूटन के किस नियम के अनुसार प्रकृति में प्रत्येक क्रिया (बल) के लिए एक समान और विपरीत प्रतिक्रिया होती है ?

[SSC GD 2024]
options_hi: दूसरे
पहले
चौथे
तीसरे
solution_hi:
हल: सही उत्तर है तीसरे

Explanation:
न्यूटन का गति का तीसरा नियम कहता है कि "प्रत्येक क्रिया के लिए एक समान और विपरीत प्रतिक्रिया होती है।" इसका अर्थ है कि जब कोई वस्तु किसी दूसरी वस्तु पर बल लगाती है, तो दूसरी वस्तु भी पहली वस्तु पर उतना ही बल विपरीत दिशा में लगाती है। उदाहरण के लिए, जब हम जमीन पर पैर से दबाव डालते हैं (क्रिया), तो जमीन भी हमारे पैर पर उतना ही बल ऊपर की ओर लगाती है (प्रतिक्रिया), जिससे हम चल पाते हैं। यह नियम रॉकेट के प्रणोदन (propulsion) और तैराकी जैसी गतियों को समझने में मदद करता है।

Extra Facts:
- न्यूटन के गति के तीन नियम हैं: पहला नियम (जड़त्व का नियम), दूसरा नियम (बल = द्रव्यमान × त्वरण), और तीसरा नियम (क्रिया-प्रतिक्रिया)।
- यह नियम संवेग संरक्षण के सिद्धांत से जुड़ा है, क्योंकि क्रिया और प्रतिक्रिया के बलों का योग शून्य होता है।
- इस नियम का उपयोग जेट इंजन, रॉकेट और यहाँ तक कि बंदूक की गोली के पीछे हटने (recoil) में भी होता है।

question:
Acceleration is equal to the rate of change of ______.

[SSC CGL 2021]
options: momentum
position
displacement
velocity
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is velocity (option d)

Explanation:
Acceleration is defined as the rate of change of velocity. Mathematically, it is expressed as:
[
a = frac{Delta v}{Delta t}
]
where,
- (a) = acceleration
- (Delta v) = change in velocity
- (Delta t) = change in time

Velocity is a vector quantity that includes both magnitude (speed) and direction. Thus, acceleration occurs when either the magnitude, direction, or both of velocity change.

Speed is a scalar quantity and only represents magnitude, making it incorrect. Position and displacement are also incorrect because acceleration is not directly related to them.

Extra Facts:
- The SI unit of acceleration is meter/second² (m/s²).
- If velocity decreases over time, it is called negative acceleration or retardation.
- Newton’s Second Law (F = ma) establishes the relationship between acceleration, force, and mass.
- Acceleration due to gravity (g ≈ 9.8 m/s²) acts on all objects near Earth’s surface.

Important one-liners for upcoming exams
☛ What is the SI unit of acceleration? → meter/second² (m/s²)
☛ What is the formula of Newton’s Second Law? → F = ma
☛ What is the value of acceleration due to gravity? → 9.8 m/s²
☛ Difference between velocity and speed? → Velocity is a vector (direction + magnitude), speed is scalar (only magnitude)
☛ What is negative acceleration called? → Retardation
question_hi:
त्वरण , _________ के परिवर्तन की दर के बराबर होता है।

[SSC CGL 2021]
options_hi: गति
स्थिति
विस्थापन
वेग
solution_hi:
हल: सही उत्तर है वेग (विकल्प d)

Explanation:
त्वरण (Acceleration) को वेग के परिवर्तन की दर के रूप में परिभाषित किया जाता है। गणितीय रूप से, इसे इस प्रकार व्यक्त किया जाता है:
[
a = frac{Delta v}{Delta t}
]
जहाँ,
- (a) = त्वरण
- (Delta v) = वेग में परिवर्तन
- (Delta t) = समय में परिवर्तन

वेग (Velocity) एक सदिश राशि है जिसमें परिमाण (गति) और दिशा दोनों शामिल होते हैं। इसलिए, त्वरण तब होता है जब वेग का परिमाण, दिशा या दोनों बदलते हैं।

गति (Speed) एक अदिश राशि है और केवल परिमाण को दर्शाती है, इसलिए यह गलत विकल्प है। स्थिति (Position) और विस्थापन (Displacement) भी गलत हैं क्योंकि त्वरण सीधे इनसे संबंधित नहीं है।

Extra Facts:
- त्वरण का SI मात्रक मीटर/सेकंड² (m/s²) है।
- यदि वेग समय के साथ घटता है, तो इसे ऋणात्मक त्वरण (Negative Acceleration) या मंदन (Retardation) कहा जाता है।
- न्यूटन का दूसरा नियम (F = ma) त्वरण, बल और द्रव्यमान के बीच संबंध स्थापित करता है।
- त्वरण गुरुत्वाकर्षण (g ≈ 9.8 m/s²) के कारण भी होता है, जो पृथ्वी की सतह पर सभी वस्तुओं पर लागू होता है।

question:
Distance covered by the object is _______to time.

[SSC CGL 2022]
options: equal proportional
directly proportional
inversely proportional
double proportional
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Directly Proportional

Explanation:
The distance covered by an object is directly proportional to time. This means if time increases, distance also increases, and vice versa. This relationship is derived from the formula of motion (Distance = Speed × Time), where distance varies directly with time when speed is constant. For example, if an object moves at 10 km/h, it covers 20 km in 2 hours and 30 km in 3 hours.

Extra Facts:
The distance-time relationship is fundamental in physics for studying motion. Newton’s Laws of Motion and graphical analysis rely on this. If speed isn’t constant (e.g., with acceleration), distance may vary with the square of time (s = ut + ½ at²). In inverse proportionality (e.g., time and speed), one quantity decreases as the other increases.

Important one-liners for upcoming exams
☛ What is the formula for speed? → Distance/Time
☛ What is the formula for acceleration? → (Final Velocity – Initial Velocity)/Time
☛ What is Newton’s First Law of Motion? → Law of Inertia
☛ How does a velocity-time graph look for constant acceleration? → Straight line
☛ What is the SI unit of distance? → Meter
question_hi:
वस्तु द्वारा तय की गई दूरी समय के _______ है।

[SSC CGL 2022]
options_hi: समान आनुपातिक
अनुक्रमानुपाती
व्यूत्क्रमानुपाती
दोहरा आनुपातिक
solution_hi:
हल: सही उत्तर है अनुक्रमानुपाती (Directly Proportional)

Explanation:
वस्तु द्वारा तय की गई दूरी समय के अनुक्रमानुपाती होती है। इसका अर्थ है कि यदि समय बढ़ता है, तो दूरी भी बढ़ती है, और यदि समय घटता है, तो दूरी भी घटती है। यह संबंध गति के सूत्र (दूरी = गति × समय) से स्पष्ट होता है, जहाँ गति स्थिर होने पर दूरी समय के सीधे अनुपात में होती है। उदाहरण के लिए, यदि कोई वस्तु 10 किमी/घंटा की गति से चलती है, तो 2 घंटे में 20 किमी और 3 घंटे में 30 किमी दूरी तय करेगी।

Extra Facts:
दूरी और समय के बीच संबंध भौतिकी में गति के अध्ययन का एक महत्वपूर्ण हिस्सा है। न्यूटन के गति के नियम और ग्राफ़िकल विश्लेषण में इस संबंध का उपयोग किया जाता है। यदि गति स्थिर नहीं है (जैसे त्वरण के साथ), तो दूरी समय के वर्ग के अनुक्रमानुपाती हो सकती है (s = ut + ½ at²)। व्यूत्क्रमानुपाती संबंध (जैसे समय और गति) में, एक राशि बढ़ने पर दूसरी घटती है।

question:
What happens to the force of gravitation between two objects when the mass of one object is doubled?

[RRB NTPC CBT]
options: The force of gravitation is tripled
The force of gravitation is halved
The force of gravitation is four times
The force of gravitation is doubled
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is The force of gravitation is doubled.

Explanation:
According to Newton's Law of Gravitation, the gravitational force (F) between two objects is directly proportional to the product of their masses (m₁ and m₂) and inversely proportional to the square of the distance (r) between them. Mathematically:
F = G (m₁ × m₂) / r²
If the mass of one object (m₁) is doubled (2m₁), the new force F' = G (2m₁ × m₂) / r² = 2 × (G m₁ m₂ / r²) = 2F. Thus, the gravitational force becomes doubled.

Extra Facts:
1. The gravitational constant (G) has a value of 6.67430 × 10⁻¹¹ N m²/kg² and is universal.
2. Gravitational force is always an attractive force and can never be repulsive.
3. On Earth, weight is a result of gravity, calculated as mass × gravitational acceleration (g = 9.8 m/s²).

Important one-liners for upcoming exams
☛ Who formulated the Universal Law of Gravitation? → Sir Isaac Newton
☛ What is the value of 'g' on Earth? → 9.8 m/s²
☛ How much is the gravitational force on the Moon compared to Earth? → 1/6th
☛ What is the unit of gravitational force? → Newton (N)
☛ What happens to gravitational force if the distance between two objects is doubled? → It becomes 1/4th
question_hi:
दो वस्तुओं में से एक का द्रव्यमान दोगुना हो जाने पर दोनों वस्तुओं के बीच लगने वाले गुरुत्वाकर्षण बल में क्या परिवर्तन होता है?

[RRB NTPC CBT]
options_hi: गुरुत्वाकर्षण बल तीन गुना हो जाता है।
गुरुत्वाकर्षण बल आधा हो जाता है।
गुरुत्वाकर्षण बल चार गुना हो जाता है।
गुरुत्वाकर्षण बल दोगुना हो जाता है।
solution_hi:
हल: सही उत्तर है गुरुत्वाकर्षण बल दोगुना हो जाता है।

Explanation:
न्यूटन के गुरुत्वाकर्षण के नियम के अनुसार, दो वस्तुओं के बीच लगने वाला गुरुत्वाकर्षण बल (F) उनके द्रव्यमानों (m₁ और m₂) के गुणनफल के समानुपाती होता है और उनके बीच की दूरी (r) के वर्ग के व्युत्क्रमानुपाती होता है। सूत्र के रूप में:
F = G (m₁ × m₂) / r²
यदि एक वस्तु का द्रव्यमान (m₁) दोगुना हो जाता है (2m₁), तो नया बल F' = G (2m₁ × m₂) / r² = 2 × (G m₁ m₂ / r²) = 2F होगा। इस प्रकार, गुरुत्वाकर्षण बल दोगुना हो जाता है।

question:
The acceleration due to gravity at the surface of the earth (mass M and radius R) is proportional to ______.

[RRB NTPC CBT]
options:
MR

MR2

M2R

MR3
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is MR2

Explanation:
The acceleration due to gravity (g) at the surface of the Earth is given by the formula:
g=GMR2
Where:
G = Universal gravitational constant (6.67 × 10-11 Nm2/kg2)
M = Mass of the Earth
R = Radius of the Earth

From this formula, it is clear that g is proportional to MR2. This is derived from Newton's Law of Gravitation, which states that the gravitational force between two objects is directly proportional to the product of their masses and inversely proportional to the square of the distance between them.

Extra Facts:
1. The average value of g at the Earth's surface is 9.8 m/s2, but it varies slightly depending on location.
2. The acceleration due to gravity is also affected by the Earth's rotation and shape.
3. On the Moon, the value of g is about 1/6th of that on Earth because the Moon has less mass and radius compared to Earth.
4. Gravitational force is what keeps us bound to the Earth and causes objects to fall downward.

question:
______ is a change of position.

[SSC CGL 2022]
options: Speed
Velocity
Motion
Distance
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Motion

Explanation:
Motion refers to the change in position of an object with respect to time. In physics, motion is defined as the change in position of an object over time. It is a vector quantity, meaning it has both magnitude and direction. Types of motion include uniform motion, non-uniform motion, circular motion, and periodic motion. Speed and Velocity are related to motion but are not motion itself. Speed is a scalar quantity (only magnitude), while velocity is a vector quantity (both magnitude and direction). Distance is simply the length between two points and does not indicate a change in position.

Extra Facts:
The laws governing motion are based on Newton's Laws of Motion. The First Law (Law of Inertia) states that an object remains in its state of motion unless acted upon by an external force. The Second Law (F=ma) relates force, mass, and acceleration. The Third Law (Action-Reaction) states that every action has an equal and opposite reaction. The study of motion is divided into kinematics (description of motion) and dynamics (causes of motion). Motion is fundamental in understanding various phenomena in mechanics, astronomy, and engineering.

question:
The measure of the force that can cause an object to rotate about an axis is called:

[SSC CPO 2024]
options: power
moment of inertia
centripetal force
torque
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is torque

Explanation:
Torque is the measure of the force that can cause an object to rotate about an axis. It is the product of the force and the perpendicular distance (lever arm) from the axis of rotation to the line of action of the force. The formula is:
τ = r × F × sinθ
where,
τ = torque,
r = distance from the pivot point,
F = applied force,
θ = angle between force and distance.
Its SI unit is Newton-meter (N·m). Torque is commonly observed in daily life, such as in bicycle pedals, door handles, and screwdrivers.

Extra Facts:
Moment of Inertia measures an object's resistance to rotational motion, while Centripetal Force is required to keep an object moving in a circular path. Power represents the rate of doing work. The relationship between torque and angular acceleration is given by τ = Iα, where I is the moment of inertia and α is angular acceleration.

☛ What is moment of inertia? → Resistance to rotational motion
☛ In which direction does centripetal force act? → Towards the center of the circle
☛ What is the SI unit of power? → Watt (W)
☛ What is the formula for angular momentum? → L = Iω

Extra Facts:
जड़त्व आघूर्ण (Moment of Inertia) किसी वस्तु के घूर्णी गति का विरोध करने की प्रवृत्ति को दर्शाता है, जबकि अभिकेंद्र बल (Centripetal Force) किसी वस्तु को वृत्तीय पथ पर गतिमान रखने के लिए आवश्यक बल है। शक्ति (Power) कार्य करने की दर को दर्शाती है। बलाघूर्ण और कोणीय त्वरण के बीच संबंध τ = Iα से दिया जाता है, जहाँ I जड़त्व आघूर्ण और α कोणीय त्वरण है।

question:
If the mass of a person is 60 kg on the surface of earth then the same person‘s mass on the surface of the moon will be:

[RRB NTPC CBT]
options: 0 kg
360 kg
60 kg
10 kg
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is 60 kg

Explanation:
Mass is a measure of the amount of matter in an object and remains constant regardless of the object's location. The amount of matter (mass) in a person's body remains the same on Earth or the Moon. However, the gravitational force on the Moon is about 1/6th of that on Earth, which causes the person's weight to be less on the Moon, but the mass remains unchanged. Therefore, the person's mass on the Moon will still be 60 kg.

Extra Facts:

- Weight is a vector quantity that depends on gravitational force, and its SI unit is Newton (N).
- The gravitational acceleration (g) on the Moon is about 1/6th of Earth's g, i.e., ~1.62 m/s².
- According to Newton's Law of Gravitation, F = G (m1m2)/r², where G is the gravitational constant.

question:

solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is m/s2

Explanation:
Acceleration is the rate of change of velocity with respect to time. Its SI unit is meter per second squared (m/s2). This unit is derived because acceleration is calculated by dividing the change in velocity (m/s) by time (s). Other options like ft/s (feet per second) and m/s (meter per second) are units of velocity, while sqm/s (square meter per second) is not a valid physical unit.

Extra Facts:
Acceleration is a vector quantity, meaning it has both magnitude and direction. According to Newton's Second Law (F = ma), the force applied on an object equals its mass (m) multiplied by acceleration (a). Negative acceleration is called retardation, indicating a decrease in velocity. The gravitational acceleration (g) on Earth's surface is approximately 9.8 m/s2.

question:
Which is the least frictional force of the following?

[RRB NTPC CBT]
options: Sliding
Fluid
Static
Rolling
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Rolling

Explanation:
Frictional force is the force that opposes the relative motion between two surfaces. It is of four types: Static friction (when the object is at rest), Sliding friction (when the object slides), Rolling friction (when the object rolls), and Fluid friction (when the object moves through a fluid). Among these, rolling friction is the least because rolling involves minimal contact surface and energy dissipation. Static friction is the highest as it must be overcome to initiate motion.

Extra Facts:
The formula for frictional force is F = μN, where μ is the coefficient of friction and N is the normal force. The coefficient of rolling friction (μrolling) is much lower than sliding (μsliding) and static friction (μstatic). This is why wheels are used in transportation to save energy. Fluid friction depends on the object's shape and the viscosity of the fluid.

Important one-liners for upcoming exams

☛ Which type of frictional force is the highest? → Static friction
☛ What type of friction occurs in wheels? → Rolling friction
☛ What is the direction of frictional force? → Opposite to the direction of motion
☛ What is used to reduce friction? → Lubricants

question:
What kind of energy does a yo-yo have before it is released ?

[SSC CPO 2024]
options: Potential energy
Light energy
Chemical energy
Kinetic energy
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Potential energy

Explanation:
Before a yo-yo is released, it possesses potential energy. According to the law of conservation of energy, when the yo-yo is pulled up, its height increases, storing potential energy due to its position against the gravitational force. This energy is calculated using the formula PE = mgh, where m is mass, g is acceleration due to gravity, and h is height. When the yo-yo is released, this potential energy converts into kinetic energy as it moves downward.

Extra Facts:
Potential energy is of two types: gravitational potential energy and elastic potential energy. Gravitational potential energy is due to an object's height, while elastic potential energy arises from deformation (like stretching or compressing a spring). The law of conservation of energy states that energy cannot be created or destroyed, only transformed from one form to another. This principle is fundamental in physics and applies to all energy interactions.

यो-यो के रिलीज़ होने से पहले इसमें स्थितिज उर्जा (Potential Energy) होती है। ऊर्जा के संरक्षण के नियम के अनुसार, जब यो-यो को ऊपर खींचा जाता है, तो उसकी ऊंचाई बढ़ने के कारण उसमें स्थितिज उर्जा संचित हो जाती है। यह उर्जा गुरुत्वाकर्षण बल के विरुद्ध कार्य करने के कारण उत्पन्न होती है। जब यो-यो को छोड़ा जाता है, तो यह स्थितिज उर्जा गतिज उर्जा (Kinetic Energy) में परिवर्तित हो जाती है। स्थितिज उर्जा की गणना सूत्र PE = mgh से की जाती है, जहाँ m द्रव्यमान, g गुरुत्वाकर्षण के कारण त्वरण, और h ऊंचाई है।

question:
Motion of an object is ______ if its velocity is constant.

[SSC CGL 2022]
options: only accelerating
only decelerating
non-uniform
uniform
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is uniform

Explanation:
When an object has constant velocity, its motion is called uniform. Velocity is a vector quantity that includes both magnitude (speed) and direction. If velocity is constant, it means neither the speed nor the direction is changing. Thus, the object's motion is uniform. According to Newton's First Law of Motion, if no external force is applied, an object continues its uniform motion.

Extra Facts:
There is a difference between uniform speed and uniform velocity. Uniform speed means only the magnitude is constant, while uniform velocity means both magnitude and direction are constant. In uniform circular motion, speed remains constant, but the direction continuously changes, making it an example of non-uniform motion. The branch of science that studies motion is called kinematics.

question:
When one stone is thrown upwards, what type of energy conversion would occur ?

[RRB NTPC CBT]
options: Kinetic energy would change to mechanical energy
Potential energy would change to gravitational energy
Mechanical energy would change to kinetic energy
Kinetic energy would change to gravitational potential energy
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Kinetic energy would change to gravitational potential energy

Explanation:
When a stone is thrown upwards, its kinetic energy gradually converts into gravitational potential energy due to the gravitational force. As the stone moves upward, its speed decreases, and its height increases, leading to an increase in potential energy. According to the law of conservation of energy, the total mechanical energy (kinetic + potential) remains constant, but the form of energy changes.

Extra Facts:
The formula for gravitational potential energy is: U = mgh, where m is mass, g is gravitational acceleration (9.8 m/s²), and h is height. The formula for kinetic energy is: K = ½mv², where v is velocity. At the highest point, the stone's velocity becomes zero, and all its kinetic energy is converted into potential energy. This process reverses when the stone falls back down.

question:
12. The rate of doing work is called:

[SSC CGL 2021]
options: impulse
force
power
energy
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is power

Explanation:
The rate of doing work is called power. In physics, power is defined as the rate at which work is done or energy is transferred. Its SI unit is the watt (W), which can also be expressed as joules per second (J/s). The formula to calculate power is: P = W/t, where P is power, W is work done, and t is time. For example, if a machine does 100 joules of work in 5 seconds, its power would be 20 watts. Power is a scalar quantity, meaning it has only magnitude and no direction.

Extra Facts:
Other units of power include horsepower (HP), which is still used to measure the power of vehicles and machines. 1 HP is approximately equal to 746 watts. For electrical power, the formula P = VI is used, where V is voltage and I is current. The concept of power is crucial in daily life, such as the power ratings of electrical appliances, which indicate their energy consumption.

question:
The motion of the body moving along a circular path is an example of_______.

[SSC CGL 2022]
options: decelerated motion
accelerated motion
non-uniform motion
uniform motion
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is accelerated motion

Explanation:
The motion of a body moving along a circular path is an example of accelerated motion, even if the speed of the body is constant. This is because the direction of the body continuously changes, causing its velocity to change as well. According to Newton's second law of motion, a change in velocity means acceleration. This acceleration acts towards the center of the circle and is called centripetal acceleration. The formula for centripetal acceleration is: ( a = frac{v^2}{r} ), where ( v ) is the speed of the object and ( r ) is the radius of the circle.

Extra Facts:
1. Centripetal Force: The force required for circular motion that pulls the object towards the center of the circle. Its formula is: ( F = frac{mv^2}{r} ), where ( m ) is the mass of the object.
2. Examples: Earth's revolution around the Sun, an electron orbiting the nucleus, or a car moving on a circular track.
3. Uniform Circular Motion: If the speed of the object is constant, it is called uniform circular motion, but it is still accelerated motion because the direction changes continuously.

Important one-liners for upcoming exams
☛ What is Newton's Second Law of Motion? → Force = Mass × Acceleration (F = ma)
☛ What is the formula for centripetal acceleration? → ( a = frac{v^2}{r} )
☛ What remains constant in uniform circular motion? → Speed
☛ What type of motion is Earth's revolution around the Sun? → Accelerated motion
☛ What is the direction of centripetal force? → Towards the center of the circle

question:
The force of attraction between all masses in the universe, especially the attraction of the earth's mass for bodies near its surface is called-

[RRB NTPC CBT]
options: Mechanical force
Gravitational force
Friction force
Spring force
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Gravitational force

Explanation:
The force of attraction between all masses in the universe is called gravitational force. This force operates according to the Universal Law of Gravitation proposed by Sir Isaac Newton. According to this law, the attractive force between two objects is directly proportional to the product of their masses and inversely proportional to the square of the distance between them. The attraction exerted by the Earth's mass on bodies near its surface is called gravitational force, which causes objects to fall towards the Earth. The unit of this force is Newton (N).

Extra Facts:
1. The gravitational force was discovered by Sir Isaac Newton in 1687.
2. The value of Earth's gravitational acceleration (g) is approximately 9.8 m/s².

4. Due to gravitational force, the Earth revolves around the Sun and the Moon revolves around the Earth.

question:
Newton is the unit to measure _______.

[RRB NTPC CBT]
options: pressure
resistance
force
power
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is force

Explanation:
The newton (N) is the International System of Units (SI) derived unit of force. It is named after Sir Isaac Newton, who formulated the laws of motion and universal gravitation. Mathematically, 1 N = 1 kg·m/s², meaning that one newton is the force required to accelerate a mass of one kilogram at a rate of one meter per second squared. This unit is used to measure various forces, including gravitational force, frictional force, and applied forces in physics.

Extra Facts:
Force is a vector quantity, possessing both magnitude and direction. Newton's three laws of motion form the foundation of classical mechanics:
1. Law of Inertia – An object remains at rest or in uniform motion unless acted upon by an external force.
2. Force-Acceleration Law – Force = mass × acceleration (F = ma).
3. Action-Reaction Law – For every action, there is an equal and opposite reaction.

solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Kgm/ sec²

Explanation:
According to the definition of Work, Work = Force × Displacement (in the direction of force). The SI unit of work is Joule (J), which is equivalent to Newton-meter (N·m).

In the options:

- Newton meter: This is also a unit of work, as 1 Newton-meter = 1 Joule.
- Joule: This is the standard SI unit of work.

However, Kgm/ sec² is the unit of Force, not work. The SI unit of force is Newton (N), which is equal to 1 kg·m/s². Hence, this is not a unit of work.

Extra Facts:
- Work is a scalar quantity, and its unit is Joule.
- 1 Joule = 1 Newton × 1 meter = 1 kg·m²/s².
- Power is the rate of doing work, and its unit is Watt (W). 1 Watt = 1 Joule/second.
- The units of Energy and Work are the same, as both represent the same physical quantity.

question_hi:
किसी वस्तु पर कार्य करने वाले बल द्वारा किया गया कार्य बल की दिशा में तय की गई दूरी से गुणा किए गए बल की मात्रा के बराबर होता है। निम्नलिखित में से कौन कार्य का मात्रक नहीं है?

[RRB NTPC CBT]
options_hi: Kgm²/Sec²
Kgm/ sec²
न्यूटन मीटर
जूल
solution_hi:
हल: सही उत्तर है Kgm/ sec²

Explanation:
कार्य (Work) की परिभाषा के अनुसार, कार्य = बल × विस्थापन (बल की दिशा में)। कार्य का SI मात्रक जूल (Joule) है, जो न्यूटन-मीटर (N·m) के बराबर होता है।

विकल्पों में:
- Kgm²/Sec²: यह जूल (Joule) के समतुल्य है, क्योंकि 1 जूल = 1 किग्रा·मी²/सेकंड²।
- न्यूटन मीटर: यह भी कार्य का मात्रक है, क्योंकि 1 न्यूटन-मीटर = 1 जूल।
- जूल: यह कार्य का मानक SI मात्रक है।

लेकिन Kgm/ sec² बल (Force) का मात्रक है, न कि कार्य का। बल का SI मात्रक न्यूटन (N) है, जो 1 किग्रा·मी/सेकंड² के बराबर होता है। इसलिए, यह कार्य का मात्रक नहीं है।

Extra Facts:
- कार्य एक अदिश राशि है, जिसका मात्रक जूल होता है।
- 1 जूल = 1 न्यूटन × 1 मीटर = 1 किग्रा·मी²/सेकंड²।
- शक्ति (Power) कार्य करने की दर है, जिसका मात्रक वाट (Watt) होता है। 1 वाट = 1 जूल/सेकंड।
- ऊर्जा और कार्य के मात्रक समान होते हैं, क्योंकि दोनों एक ही भौतिक राशि को दर्शाते हैं।
